jobs.occupation: Head of International Markets and Regulatory Operations
jobs.description:
Don’t just lead regulatory delivery. Shape regulatory impact and operational excellence across borders. This is a unique role combining leadership of our Regulatory Affiliate teams across our International Markets with the opportunity to lead and shape LEO Pharma’s Global Regulatory Operations capabilities —building stronger connected teams, smarter ways of working and greater business impact.

Join us in creating a future legacy in medical dermatology

At LEO Pharma, we are global leaders in medical dermatology. We have 118 years’ experience in bringing innovation to healthcare. And we are eager to do much more. Each year, close to 100 million people have a better day because of our medicines. In this role, you will bring international regulatory leadership and global operations together—with the opportunity to shape how teams, partners, data and systems deliver across markets.

At LEO Pharma, how we work matters. We build trusted relationships and deliver with impact. We focus on where we can make the greatest difference and have the courage to explore new possibilities. We collaborate across boundaries and take accountability for our part. Here, you can grow, contribute with confidence, and make a meaningful difference together with others.

Your role

You will provide strategic and operational leadership for International Markets outside North America and Global Regulatory Operations. Your mission is to set the strategic direction for regulatory affairs across our International Markets while driving global operational excellence through LEO Pharma’s Regulatory Operations capabilities. By uniting strong affiliate leadership with a high-performing global operating model, you will strengthen regulatory impact, enable business priorities and build the capabilities needed for sustainable regulatory delivery and performance across our portfolio.

Your key responsibilities will be to:

• Lead International Markets Regulatory Affairs, strengthening country leadership, regulatory intelligence and Health Authority relationships.

• Align portfolio lifecycle delivery with market priorities, enabling timely, compliant new pipeline product introductions, geographic expansion, regulatory operations and maintenance and supporting the Established/Core Portfolio and Critical Care franchises.

• Shape regulatory data and systems strategy, advancing automation and appropriate AI-enabled capabilities.

• Direct portfolio planning, resource allocation, budgets and performance management, simplifying processes and improving delivery.

• Build accountable vendor partnerships while maintaining quality, compliance and inspection readiness across internal and outsourced activities.

This is an opportunity to shape an innovative and integrated regulatory operating model—strengthening affiliate leadership and advancing global operational excellence, digital capabilities and strategic partnerships to deliver sustainable, compliant business impact in a forward-looking regulatory organisation.

Your qualifications

You bring scientific grounding, substantial regulatory leadership experience and the expertise to connect strategy with execution. We imagine that you have:

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biomedicine, chemistry or another relevant scientific discipline.

• At least 10 years of pharmaceutical industry experience, including substantial regulatory leadership, with demonstrated ability to connect market priorities with operational execution through strong expereince in one area and sound understanding of the other.

• Broad knowledge of international and European regulatory frameworks across development, registration and post-approval lifecycle management.

• Significant expertise in regulatory operations, data, systems, compliance, outsourcing, vendor governance and digital transformation.

• A track record of organisational transformation, talent development and senior stakeholder influence, supported by strong commercial and financial acumen.

You think globally, communicate clearly and bring decisive leadership to complex situations. You empower others while maintaining accountability, with patients, customers and quality at the heart of your decisions.

Your new team

You will join Global Regulatory Affairs, reporting to the VP, Global Regulatory Affairs, with approximately 10 direct reports. Your geographically dispersed organisation connects market teams with regulatory business operations, data, systems and digital capabilities. Working closely with Development, Commercial and other Enterprise stakeholders, you will foster collaboration, develop talent and lead new ways of working.

Application

You do not need to upload a cover letter, but feel free to add a few sentences in your resume or CV on why this position has your interest. Please refrain from adding a photo to your CV.

Curiosity Beyond

Our Curiosity Beyond program reflects our belief that embracing differences creates a workplace where we can all thrive and innovate. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, age, disability, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristics. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants. Candidates who require accommodation during the recruitment process or at work are encouraged to contact Talent Acquisition to discuss their needs.

LEO Pharma is a global leader in medical dermatology. We deliver innovative solutions for skin health, building on a century of experience with breakthrough medicines in healthcare. We are committed to making a fundamental difference in people’s lives, and our broad portfolio of treatments serves close to 100 million patients in over 70 countries annually.

Join us in this role where you’ll help develop and maintain the planning models used across Finance, translate business needs into practical solutions, and support planning and forecasting cycles. You’ll build expertise across FP&A, data, and modern planning technology while gradually taking ownership of your own areas.

Welcome to Financial Business Intelligence

You’ll be part of Financial Business Intelligence where you, together with your colleagues, will develop and support the planning solutions used across Finance. You’ll work with experienced finance, data, and reporting specialists to turn requirements and financial drivers into reliable models and better ways of working. As a team, we share knowledge, solve problems together, and give you space to learn, contribute, and grow.

You’ll play an important role in:

• 
supporting the development and maintenance of FP&A planning models

• 
translating Finance requirements into practical planning solutions

• 
improving planning and forecasting processes through data and digital tools

• 
working with financial drivers and data used in planning models

• 
supporting Finance colleagues during planning and forecasting cycles

• 
testing, documenting, and continuously improving planning solutions.

To succeed in the role, you:

• 
have a relevant degree in Finance, Economics, Business, or a similar field, or equivalent experience

• 
understand core financial concepts and are comfortable working with numbers and data

• 
bring experience from, or a strong interest in, Finance, controlling, FP&A, accounting, or business analysis

• 
are curious about how digital tools can improve Finance processes and decision-making

• 
work in a structured way, learn quickly, and take responsibility for your own tasks

• 
communicate clearly and collaborate well with both Finance colleagues and technical specialists.

Experience with SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP BPC, Power BI, or similar tools is an advantage. More important is your financial understanding, curiosity, and motivation to develop your digital skills.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

Location: Gentofte, Denmark

**Position salary range:

**For this position, the expected base pay range is kr41,000.00- kr61,000.00 for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Our benefits package:

**For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11% contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3% holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and wellbeing programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

**Pre-employment background check:

**Certain positions may require a background check as part of the hiring process. If applicable, you will be informed during the recruitment process. Background checks are conducted by an external provider in accordance with local legal requirements.

Imagine a future with Ørsted

Join a global leader in renewable energy

Ørsted is a global leader in offshore wind and is one of the largest renewable energy companies in the world. With us, you’ll play your part in creating a world that runs entirely on green energy. As a leading green energy company, we leverage the curiosity and passion of our people to innovate and develop new technologies or bring existing technologies to scale, collaborating with governments, suppliers, and our industry partners to make renewable energy solutions a reality. At Ørsted, we work together with openness and respect and seek fresh perspectives to solve any task at hand: big or small.

**About Ørsted

**

• We provide countries, companies, and communities with sustainable, reliable, and cost-competitive energy solutions, including offshore and onshore wind, solar PV, and energy storage.

• Our vision is to create a world that runs entirely on green energy.

• We built the world’s first offshore wind farm, Vindeby in Denmark, in 1991, and completed the world’s largest, Hornsea 2 in the UK, in 2022.

• We were founded in Denmark in 2006 and now have approximately 8,000 employees, working in 15 countries and counting.

An inclusive team

At Ørsted, we strive to be an inclusive workplace where you’re respected for who you are, valued for the unique perspectives you bring, and rewarded fairly for what you achieve. We want all employees to have the same opportunities for impact and growth, no matter their age, race, ethnicity, place of birth, gender, sexual orientation, or disability.

Most go-to-market teams stop training people the day ramp ends. Onboarding is a slide deck and a week of shadowing. Coaching happens when a manager finds time. Practice tools get bought, and nobody opens them after week one.

We're building the opposite: a system that makes everyone in go-to-market better every week, from their first day to their hundredth customer. We start with sales, then take it to every GTM team. Onboarding that runs on time. Practice that is assigned, scored and reviewed. Feedback from real calls, one behaviour at a time. Managers who coach from data, not memory.

If you'd rather build the machine that makes people better than run another training session, keep reading.

🥞 The mission

All Gravy is the frontline operating system.

One platform for everything from comms to learning to handbooks and checklists, with built-in AI. Think Instagram meets Duolingo for frontline workers.

Used daily by brands like GAIL's, Dishoom, 7-Eleven and Honest Burgers.

We're growing 3x year-over-year, backed by Moonfire, Scale Capital and operators who've built billion-dollar companies. We're hiring, scaling fast, and the best is yet to come. 🚀

🎯 The role

Revenue Effectiveness is a new lane in our Revenue Engineering team. Imagine traditional Enablement and modern Revenue Operations joined forces: that’s this role. You own how our go-to-market people get good and stay good, across every GTM function. SDRs and AEs first, then customer success, solutions engineering and beyond

• 
Onboarding. Every new hire goes through the same programme for their role, on time, with clear gates. For sales, our ramp target, the 90-Day Ladder, is about 2.5x faster than our historical curve.

• 
Continuous training. Ramp ends; training doesn't. People keep practising specific behaviours, and the practice is scored and reviewed.

• 
Coaching support for first-line managers. Managers coach. You give them the system, the data and the drills to do it well.

• 
Change management. When we ship new tools, plays or processes, you make sure they land and get used.

You work hand in hand with GTM leadership and the managers. You don't carry a quota and you don't manage the teams. You're accountable for how fast people ramp and how much better they get.

Role split:

• 
50% build: the programme, scorecards, practice bots and coaching loops, and the AI agents that run them

• 
35% run: onboarding cohorts, feedback sessions, call reviews and manager support

• 
15% change: rollouts, adoption, and measuring what stuck

🧠 What you'll build

• 
Onboarding that runs itself. A confirmed hire goes in. Accounts, calendar, practice and reviews follow without anyone chasing.

• 
Practice that's assigned, not optional. AI roleplay with narrow scorecards for each behaviour, due dates and a clear bar.

• 
Coaching from real calls. AI call scoring tuned so a score means something, with feedback on one behaviour at a time.

• 
Coaching loops for managers. Every manager sees who's stuck on what, and gets the drill that fixes it.

• 
A ramp you can measure. Practice volume, pass rates and live-call quality against the 90-Day Ladder, in one place.

• 
SPIN and MEDDPICC in practice. Stage criteria and next-step discipline, coached in every review, not left on a slide.

👋 You'll thrive here if you

• 
Have 3+ years in sales enablement, sales training or first-line sales leadership, and you've owned onboarding and coaching

• 
Can prove you made people better: faster ramp, higher conversion, better quota attainment, stronger retention. With numbers!

• 
Build systems, not decks. You're at home with AI tools and data, and you'd rather automate a process than run it by hand twice

• 
Love the craft of coaching. Listening to calls, spotting the pattern, turning it into a drill

• 
Earn trust with reps and managers alike. You push people because you believe in them

• 
Measure what you do, and change course when the data says so

• 
Speak excellent English (we work across the Nordics, UK, Germany and beyond)

⚡ Why here (the unfair advantages)

• 
The stack is already built. AI call scoring, AI roleplay, and a GTM Suite we build in-house, with a Revenue Engineering team that ships every week.

• 
Clear methods. SPIN for discovery, MEDDPICC for qualification and close. Enforced, not optional.

• 
Leadership that wants it. Continuous training is a requirement here, not a nice-to-have.

• 
A product frontline teams actually love. Our sellers aren't pushing; they're pulling interested buyers through.

📈 Where this goes

• 
3 months: Every new sales hire runs the same onboarding. Practice is assigned and reviewed, and managers get a weekly view of who needs what.

• 
6 months: Continuous training runs for the whole sales team. Ramp time is measured and coming down.

• 
12 months: The model runs across every GTM team, customer success and solutions engineering included, and scales to new markets and segments as the team grows several times over.

• 
Beyond: You lead the Effectivness team as it grows.

💰 The money

• 
Salary: 600.000 - 840.000 DKK

• 
Warrants package: when All Gravy grows, you grow with it.

• 
Pension & health insurance

💎 Perks & vibes

• 
A tight, kind, ambitious team that likes winning (and lunch).

• 
High-pace, high-trust environment with ex-founders and scale-up pros.

• 
Autonomy, coaching, and room to experiment.

• 
Snacks & beers (mainly on Fridays 😉) and a stocked fridge.

• 
Team events: socials, offsites, padel, and the occasional wine tasting.

• 
Learning culture: we practice feedback and give you responsibility so you can grow fast.

🙌 Ready to own it?

If you want to build the system that makes people genuinely better every week, and keeps them improving long after ramp, apply.

Bonus points if your application tells us about one person you made measurably better. What did you change? How did you know it worked? What would you automate today?

We're 70+ people today. Come grow with us. 💥

Copenhagen · In the office 5 days a week, with flexibility agreed with your manager · Full-time · Start: as soon as possible

Languages: English required

KIME is expanding its Go to Market and Solutions teams: Account Executives, BDRs, customer success and AI Strategists, all working in HubSpot and enabled by RevOps. As our RevOps Manager, you make that team run on clean data and report on the KPIs.

About KIME

KIME is AI search visibility software for brands. Our agentic platform shows companies how they appear in ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Mode, Perplexity, Claude and Grok, and what to change to get recommended. AI is becoming where buyers discover brands, and most companies are not ready. We are currently based in Copenhagen and Stockholm, working with brands across the Nordics, Europe, and the United States.

What you will own

The systems and numbers behind KIME's revenue. You own HubSpot, the weekly forecast and reporting, and the commission plans for every commercial role. You support our sales leadership and lead our RevOps Associate.

What you will do

• 
Own HubSpot. Pipelines, properties, workflows, lead routing and data quality, built so sales can move fast and leadership can trust the numbers.

• 
Run the forecast. Build the weekly pipeline and forecast view with our sales leadership, and report on it to the founders.

• 
Run commission plans. Calculate commission for AEs, BDRs, CSMs, and AI Strategists, with transparent rules everyone understands.

• 
Route and qualify. Keep territories, lead routing and our ideal customer scoring working as we open new markets.

• 
Connect the tools. Keep the toolstack working together, and automate repeat work, using AI where it helps.

• 
Lead and coach. Lead our RevOps Associate and help them grow.

What success looks like

• 
First 30 days: you know our setup and its gaps, you have met every commercial role, and the weekly forecast runs smoothly

• 
First 90 days: commission for every role is calculated with transparent rules, and the three biggest data problems are fixed

• 
After 12 months: leadership runs the business on your dashboards, new hires and markets are set up in days, and commission is paid correctly and on time

• 
You are measured on: forecast accuracy, data quality, commission paid correctly and on time, and time saved for the commercial team

Who you are

Must-haves:

• 
4+ years in revenue operations or sales operations at a B2B SaaS company

• 
Hands-on CRM administration: you have built pipelines, properties and workflows yourself

• 
You have built a forecast and reporting that leadership used every week

• 
You have designed or run commission plans

• 
Precise with numbers, and clear when you explain them to sellers; fluent English

Nice to have:

• 
Experience at a start-up or scale-up that was growing its sales team

• 
SQL, or experience with a BI tool

• 
Danish, Swedish or another Nordic language

• 
Native in HubSpot

If you match most of this but not all, apply anyway.

Team and reporting line

You join our Go to Market team and report to our sales leadership. You lead our RevOps team and work closely with the extended commercial organization as well as and FinOps.

What we offer

• 
A high-growth team where you take real responsibility from day one

• 
A vibrant office culture and an international community

• 
A great office location in Copenhagen

Hiring process

• 
Application review

• 
20-minute intro call

• 
Interview(s) about systems you have built, and how you would approach our setup

• 
Then you meet the team, and we check references

• 
Offer, within about 3 weeks of applying

How to apply

Apply using the button on this page. No cover letter. Instead, answer one question in the form: tell us in three sentences about a revenue process or system you built: what was broken, what you built, and what changed in the numbers. Send questions to below email address.

For more information or questions please contact us at jobs@kime.ai

jobs.occupation: Spanish Speaking Business Development Analyst for our Copenhagen Office
jobs.description:
Do you want to work in an ambitious and fast-growing international company while studying? Are you motivated by taking responsibility, working strategically, and gaining hands-on experience in business development? Then this might be the right opportunity for you.

What we offer

At JUC, you will gain practical experience in international business development within a professional B2B environment.

We offer:

• Thorough onboarding and close sparring with experienced colleagues

• Insight into strategic market development and partnership building

• A dynamic and international working environment

• Real responsibility and the opportunity to influence projects

• A career-relevant student position that will significantly strengthen your professional profile

• A central workplace in Copenhagen at Axelborg, just across from Tivoli

• Friday breakfast, social events, and company celebrations

• An in-house gourmet chef serving daily lunch

This is a unique opportunity to combine your studies with relevant, hands-on experience in an international growth company.

Your new role

As a Business Development Analyst at JUC, you will become part of our Network Development department and contribute to strengthening our position in the Spanish market.

You will develop legal education programs and networks, directly focused on the Spanish market. This includes conducting market research, identifying relevant industries and professional segments, and helping translate insights into concrete business opportunities.

You will assist with outreach and preparation of meetings with high-profile lawyers and judges in connection with partnership agreements and network development initiatives. You will also work closely with our Spanish sales department in Madrid to support alignment between development activities and commercial goals.

In addition, your tasks will include:

• Market research and analysis of Spanish industries and professional segments

• Mapping potential partners and key profiles

• Supporting cross-market development activities

• Ad hoc tasks across other European markets

You will be based at our headquarters in Copenhagen and work in close collaboration with colleagues across markets. The position is minimum 15 hours per week.

Your profile

We expect that you:

• Are currently enrolled in a relevant bachelor’s or master’s program

• Are fluent in Spanish (written and spoken) and comfortable communicating professionally in English

• Are proactive, curious, and eager to learn

• Feel comfortable engaging with senior professionals in a professional context

Interest in the legal sector or international business is an advantage, but not a requirement. What matters most is your drive, analytical mindset, and motivation to develop.

Who is JUC?

Founded in 2001, JUC is today Scandinavia’s leading provider of courses, professional networks, and conferences for lawyers, legal professionals, and auditors. We are represented in Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Spain.

Ready to kick-start your career in business development?

We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and look forward to receiving your application.

If you have any questions about the position, you are welcome to contact our Talent Acquisition Lead, Anna Olivia Wluka, at +45 26 66 83 30 or aow@juc.dk  or our International Business Development Manager, Kristoffer Dræby Pedersen, at kdp@juc.dk.

We are looking for a Senior Nexthink Specialist to serve as the technical and strategic lead for all Nexthink-related activities across our client’s customer base. The ideal candidate must be able to design, challenge, and accelerate customers' adoption of Nexthink as a strategic DEX platform within large enterprise organizations.

Key responsibilities

Own and lead Nexthink implementations from solution design through deployment, adoption, and value realization

Develop and drive customers' DEX strategy and roadmap

Advise enterprise customers on the optimal use of the Nexthink platform and its capabilities

Identify and drive new DEX use cases across the organization

Ensure high platform adoption and measurable business value

Act as the technical lead in complex enterprise environments

Challenge customers' existing operating model and help mature their DEX capabilities

Work closely with Sales and Consulting teams in both pre-sales and customer expansion activities.

Key requirements

The candidate must have deep, hands-on experience with:

Nexthink (core platform) (minimum 3-5 years of experience)

Nexthink Experience / Infinity Platform

End User Computing (EUC) environments

Large-scale enterprise deployments (10,000+ endpoints)

Data collection, instrumentation, and event modeling

ITSM integrations (e.g., ServiceNow)

Experience operating at architecture, implementation, and advisory level, with proven experience delivering enterprise-scale Nexthink programs

5–10+ years of experience within End User Computing (EUC), Digital Employee Experience (DEX), or IT Operations.

Comfortable facilitating workshops and discussions with IT leadership and C-level stakeholders

Proven experience defining and executing Digital Employee Experience (DEX) strategies within enterprise organizations

Strong customer-facing and stakeholder management skills

Structured, analytical, and solution-oriented

Able to translate complex technical topics into clear business outcomes.

Nice-to-have

Experience from a consulting organization, Managed Service Provider (MSP), or software vendor is highly preferred.

We are looking for a conscientious Deputy restaurant manager of our restaurant. In this role, you will be required to greet and welcome guests, tend to their questions and complaints, manage booking and appointment schedules, and promote the restaurant in different medias. 

To be a successful Deputy restaurant manager, you should provide exceptional customer service and strong leadership skills. 

Deputy restaurant manager Responsibilities: 

• 
Defining and implementing front desk procedures. 

•

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in Adipose stem cell biology
jobs.description:
The Mandrup group invites applications from outstanding candidates for a Postdoctoral position in our group based at the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit, Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark. The position is funded by the Villum Experiment programme. The position is offered for a duration of two years and will be available from 1st of February 2027 or as soon as possible before 9th of March 2027.

Project and Research Environment
The Mandrup group investigates the molecular mechanisms governing transcriptional control of adipocyte differentiation and stem cell fate in adipose tissue, with a particular focus on how niche signals are integrated at the chromatin and transcriptional level to instruct progenitor cell fate decisions. The successful candidate will be primarily embedded in a Villum Experiment-funded project, led by Senior Postdoc Babukrishna Maniyadath, addressing how signals in the adipose tissue regulate adipogenic commitment of stem cells - a question that remains largely uncharted at the molecular level. The project draws on precision co-culture systems, single-cell genomics, live-cell imaging, si/CRISPR-based perturbation, and synthetic contact-mimicking surfaces, working exclusively with primary human and mouse cells. There will also be opportunities to contribute to related projects within the group.

Job Description
The Postdoctoral Fellow will drive experimental activities across the core areas of the project and contribute to its scientific development. The position requires both intellectual independence and close collaboration within the research group.

Key responsibilities include

• 
Planning and executing experiments across the project’s core areas, with a high degree of independence and scientific rigor

• 
Applying and developing genomic, imaging, and functional perturbation approaches to address key questions in niche signaling and progenitor fate

• 
Contributing to multi-omics data generation, integration, and interpretation

• 
Contributing to experimental design and to the development of novel approaches relevant to the project’s goals

In addition, the candidate will

• 
Contribute to supervision and mentoring of students

• 
Participate in preparation of scientific publications and dissemination of results

• 
Actively contribute to a collaborative, ambitious, and supportive research environment

Qualifications
We are seeking a highly motivated candidate with a strong experimental background in cell and molecular biology and a keen interest in understanding how direct cell-cell communication shapes adipogenic fate decisions.

Required qualifications

• 
A PhD in cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, or a related field

• 
Strong background in wet lab experiment planning and execution including mammalian cell culture and molecular biology techniques.

• 
Familiarity with transcriptomics data generation and analysis

• 
Ability to independently drive research projects

• 
Strong collaborative and communication skills

• 
Proficiency in spoken and written English

In addition, the following qualifications are relevant but not required

• 
Hands-on experience with adipose biology, stromal/progenitor cell systems, or immune biology

• 
Experience in primary cells or ex vivo systems

• 
Experience with single-cell RNA-seq or single-cell ATAC-seq - from experimental design and library preparation through to bioinformatic analysis

• 
Experience with quantitative image analysis workflows

• 
Experience with biomaterial engineering, surface functionalization, or synthetic biology approaches relevant to cell–cell contact mimicry

• 
Proficiency in computational biology, bioinformatics pipelines, and R or Python for single-cell data analysis and visualization

We offer

• 
A position in a highly focused, externally funded project at the frontier of niche biology and stem cell fate control

• 
Access to state-of-the-art infrastructure within single-cell genomics, live imaging, and molecular biology

• 
An international, highly collaborative, and dynamic research environment

• 
Strong support for scientific development and career progression

• 
Competitive salary and comprehensive social benefits

The Mandrup Group
The Mandrup Group has a long-standing interest in the detailed molecular mechanisms governing transcriptional control of adipocyte differentiation. We apply a variety of sequencing-based, computational, and molecular technologies, combined with loss- and gain-of-function strategies to study the mechanisms and role of the 3D chromatin architecture, the crosstalk between enhancers in enhancer communities and the role of specific transcription factors.
You will work closely together with other postdoctoral fellows and PhD students in the group, and you will also be expected to collaborate with colleagues in the Center of Excellence in Functional Genomics and Tissue Plasticity (ATLAS) and Center of Adipocyte Signaling (ADIPOSIGN), both directed by Susanne Mandrup. Furthermore, you will be able to benefit from the many international collaborations of our group.

The Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit
The Mandrup Group is located in the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, SDU. The research unit currently hosts eight independent research groups focusing on how specific cell types regulate gene expression and how this affects the development and function of cells and tissues. Thus, our research aims to better understand how genes regulate human physiology and diseases such as obesity, fatty liver disease, cancer, and diabetes. The research unit constitutes an international, ambitious, highly dynamic, and well-equipped working environment. The unit and the department have state-of-the-art facilities for next-generation sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics, flow cytometry, mass spectrometry, metabolomics, bioimaging, cell culture, and dietary intervention and transgenic mouse models. The unit maintains strategic research alliances with Odense University Hospital (OUH). This provides a highly stimulating research environment with numerous opportunities for learning and developing new ideas.

Application deadline: 3. January 2027 at 23:59 hours local Danish time
Please see the full call, including how to apply, on www.sdu.dk

Job description
The computational science section of the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science (IMADA) at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a PhD position associated with the research project “Riemannian Computing for Symplectic Structures” funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF). The position is to be filled earliest by March 1, 2027, and latest by Sep. 1, 2027, for a period of three years. 
The project concerns Riemannian computing applications on nonlinear matrix manifolds. The successful candidate will work at the interface of Riemannian geometry, numerical linear algebra, and scientific computing, and will develop and analyze new geometric methods and efficient numerical algorithms for data processing with symplectic structures. 

IMADA has the unique feature of bringing mathematicians and computer scientists together within a single department. The department is home to many ongoing externally funded research projects and provides a vibrant environment for junior researchers across the disciplines of mathematics, computer science, AI, data science, and quantum computing.

We are seeking curious candidates with a desire to make significant contributions to science, and a specific interest in both fundamental and computational aspects of Riemannian computing on matrix manifolds. We encourage female researchers to apply.

As the project lies at the intersection of numerical analysis, Riemannian geometry and scientific computing, applicants should have a strong background in at least one of these areas and should be ready to acquire knowledge in other ones. A background spanning all three areas would be an advantage. Scientific programming skills are considered a plus. We also expect excellent spoken and written communication skills in English.

jobs.occupation: Staff scientist position at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology at SDU
jobs.description:
A position as staff scientist (A-TAP salary level) is available at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark, Odense, from 1st of March 2027. Application deadline is 10th of January 2027.

You will be part of the research groups of Associate Professors Anne Loft (https://www.sdu.dk/en/forskning/anne-loft-lab) and Søren Fisker Schmidt (https://www.sdu.dk/en/forskning/functional-genomics/medarbejdere/medarbejdere-sfs), who explore how healthy and unhealthy adipose tissue contribute to obesity-related comorbidities, such as metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), using single cell sequencing-based methods. The groups are also developing optimized tools for targeting specific cellular subpopulations within adipose tissue. Both groups are part of the Functional Genomics & Metabolism Research Unit, an international and collaborative research environment of eight independent research groups focusing on the mechanisms controlling cell plasticity in metabolism and disease.

We are looking for a highly motivated staff scientist (PhD in molecular biology, biomedicine or related fields), who will contribute to and support research activities across the two research groups and play a central role in the day-to-day management and research infrastructure of the groups. The position includes involvement in multiple research projects, implementation and support of advanced experimental and analytical methods, coordination of research-related activities, and training and guidance of students and other group members. The position may also include limited participation in teaching activities at the department.

Qualifications

We are looking for a highly motivated, organised and collaborative staff scientist with

• 
A PhD degree in life sciences (molecular biology, biomedicine or related fields)

• 
Expertise in functional omics technologies, including single-cell analyses.

• 
Experience with bioinformatics analyses of omics data.

• 
Experience with mouse work, metabolic research and histology.

• 
Strong communication, collaborative and organisational skills.

• 
Proficiency in spoken and written English.

About the Department

The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology is part of the Faculty of Science at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense. The department provides an international, interdisciplinary, and innovative research environment, bringing together researchers, technical and administrative staff, and students.

Our research focuses on the fundamental molecular, cellular, and biochemical processes underlying cellular growth, development, and interactions in living organisms. We combine advanced analytical and biochemical technologies with computational approaches to investigate gene organization, protein structure and function, and membrane composition and dynamics. Our research contributes to a deeper understanding of fundamental biological processes and the molecular mechanisms underlying diseases such as diabetes, cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, and bacterial infections.

Applications must include

• 
Cover letter describing your motivation for applying and your most relevant qualifications.

• 
CV

• 
Certificate

For further information, please contact Anne Loft (anlo@bmb.sdu.dk) or Søren Fisker Schmidt (sfs@bmb.sdu.dk).

Employment shall take place in accordance with the framework agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

Application must include cover letter, CV and certificate. All documents in connection with the application should not contain CPR number (civil registration number) – in that case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

All attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. Cover letter and CV can contain max. 5 Mb.

We recommend that you read how to apply before you apply.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.

We are now looking for a star to take on a parental leave cover as Bar & Outlet Manager, ideally starting January 5th, 2027, until September 15th, 2027.

Skills & Qualifications Needed

• 
Hospitality Experience: Strong background in hospitality, with proven experience leading a large team in a fast-paced, 5-star environment.

• 
Commercial & Financial Acumen: Solid track record in driving revenue growth, controlling costs, and optimizing labor schedules.

• 
Ownership & Collaboration: High sense of ownership with strong problem-solving skills and the ability to partner closely with the Food & Beverage Director and senior management.

• 
Leadership & People Development: Passionate about leading on the floor, empowering Shift Leaders, and coaching and developing bartenders and floor staff.

• 
Service Excellence: Familiarity with Forbes Travel Guide 5-star service standards is considered a plus.

You identify with the following

You thrive in a high pressure and dynamic environment ensuring a consistently high level of productivity and operational standards paying particular attention to details. You are a true team player, approachable and have a can-do attitude. You are a Cosmopolitan spirit with a genuine love for Copenhagen and Mother Earth.

Responsibilities

• 
Drive Revenue & Activations: Proactively identify opportunities to boost sales and increase average guest spend through upselling strategies, promotional campaigns, and on-site bar activations.

• 
Labor Cost Management: Partner with the Food & Beverage Director to forecast, review, and adjust weekly schedules based on business volume, events, and bookings - maximizing floor productivity while keeping labor costs strictly within budget.

• 
Inventory & Cost Control: Oversee stock ordering, par levels, and supplier coordination to prevent waste, control pour costs, and ensure uninterrupted service.

• 
Training & Mentoring: Actively train, coach, and develop bartenders and floor staff to Forbes 5-star standards - focusing on product knowledge, service speed, upselling techniques, and adherence to bar standards.

• 
Shift Leader Support: Provide continuous guidance and real-time support to Shift Leaders, empowering them to make confident decisions and resolve floor issues effectively.

• 
Curate the Atmosphere: Actively monitor and adjust the venue's energy, lighting, music, and overall vibe to create a welcoming environment that drives repeat visits.
